what_it_proves: A logged-in person loaded a page of the web app
what_it_cannot_prove: Which org they were working in; whether a page view created anything

what_it_proves: The object was logged from code running inside a git repo, i.e. through the SDK
what_it_cannot_prove: Whether the SDK was called directly or via the CLI (the CLI eval runner wraps the SDK)

what_it_proves: The object came from an automated CI job through the SDK
what_it_cannot_prove: Which human set it up; the user_id is just the owner of the key CI used

what_it_proves: A server-side process tagged its own source, which only code can do
what_it_cannot_prove: That the tag is standardised; it is free text written by the customer

source_columns: raw_experiments / raw_datasets / raw_prompts with no repo_info and no source tag
what_it_proves: A person or key created something in this project
what_it_cannot_prove: Whether it was made in the UI or by the SDK outside a git repo

what_it_proves: The person opened the CLI setup wizard in the browser
what_it_cannot_prove: That the CLI was ever installed or run

what_it_proves: The person named an API key after the CLI
what_it_cannot_prove: Anything; key names are free text

what_it_proves: The person copied or clicked the MCP install command in the docs
what_it_cannot_prove: That an MCP client ever connected or made a call

what_it_proves: The org is sending production traces programmatically
what_it_cannot_prove: Which member, key or surface sent them; there is no user_id
